key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% versus bare SA516 steel, delivering the best oxidation resistance among the tested coatings.
engineering_relevance: Ni–Cr-based coatings could improve boiler-steel oxidation protection through dense protective oxide scales, reduced porosity, and increased microhardness.
method: Apply Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterize microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: Laboratory testing showed severe oxide spalling and cracking on bare steel, while protective coating scales contained Cr2O3, TiO2, NiTiO4, and NiO.
watch_item: Performance over 50 laboratory cycles does not establish long-term durability under actual boiler atmospheres and service loads.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
